title: Fix: undo/redo passes empty BlockTable — ModifyBlockDef silently no-ops
description:
## Problem
In src/main.rs:158 and :172, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y construct a throwaway empty BlockTable via Default::default() and pass it to history.undo/redo. The ModifyBlockDef arm does block_table.get_mut(*block_id) on this empty table, always gets None, and silently skips the restore. Block editing undo/redo appears to work (returns Some label, triggers redraw) but the block definition never changes.

## Root Cause
ForgeApp (src/app.rs) has no block_table field. The signature change to undo()/redo() in PR#41 added a &mut BlockTable parameter with no owner on ForgeApp.

## Fix
1. Add block_table: BlockTable to ForgeApp struct in src/app.rs
2. Initialize it in ForgeApp::new()
3. Pass &mut state.app.block_table to both undo() and redo() calls in src/main.rs:158 and :172
4. Add integration test: save → undo → assert block entities reverted

## Acceptance Criteria
- Undoing a block edit (Edit Block transaction) restores the pre-edit block definition
- Redoing restores the post-edit definition
- All 669+ tests still pass
close_reason: Fix: added block_table: BlockTable to ForgeApp struct, removing throwaway Default::default() empty tables from undo/redo. ModifyBlockDef ops now find block definitions and properly restore them. 669 tests passing.

title: Fix: Draw commands (LINE, CIRCLE, etc.) fail to commit — Confirm input never reaches active command
description:
## Summary
Clicking toolbar draw command buttons (LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, PLINE) and placing points in the viewport never commits the command because  (Enter key) is silently dropped in the action dispatch loop in . Additionally, the egui command-line text field swallows empty Enter presses without dispatching a Confirm signal.

## Root Cause

**Fault 1 — Confirm dropped at dispatch level** ():
When a draw command is active (e.g. LINE with 2+ points buffered), pressing Enter generates  from the input mapper. But the action dispatch loop's catch-all  silently discards it. The LINE command uses a buffer-then-commit design: it accumulates points on click and waits for  to spawn entities. That Confirm never arrives.

**Fault 2 — Empty Enter swallowed by egui** ():
When the command-line text field has focus and the user presses Enter with an empty buffer,  returns  and  is never set. The egui event is consumed but nothing happens.

**Fault 3 — Empty text not treated as Confirm** ():
When empty text does reach , it becomes  which hits the catch-all error in  ().

## Fix

Three coordinated changes:
1. ****: Add dedicated  handler that forwards  to the active command.
2. ****: When the command is active and the buffer is empty on Enter, dispatch an empty string as a Confirm signal to .

title: Step 11 — egui UI Panels (Status Bar, Command Line, Toolbar, Property Panel)
description:
## Context Brief

The UI system (§9) uses egui 0.34 as a post-render overlay:
- `UiSystem` holds `egui_ctx: egui::Context` and `egui_state: egui_winit::State`
- `new(window)` creates the context and state (with scale factor from window)
- `run(window, app)` takes egui input, runs the UI, returns clipped primitives
- `set_scale_factor(scale_factor)` updates pixels per point

Four panels (§9.1–9.3):
- **Status Bar** (`status_bar::draw`): Bottom panel (28px). Shows X/Y coordinates from `InputState.mouse_world`, zoom percentage from `CameraState.zoom`, and "Forge v0.1.0" label on the right.
- **Command Line** (`command_line::draw`): Bottom panel (32px), above status bar. Shows prompt from active command or "Type command:", red error text from `last_error`, and `text_edit_singleline` for input. Enter saves to `history`, sets `pending_dispatch`, clears buffer. Escape clears buffer.
- **Toolbar** (`toolbar::draw`): Left side panel (40px). Placeholder icons as labels.
- **Property Panel** (`property_panel::draw`): Right side panel (180px). Stub heading "(stub — v0.2.0+)".

Panel ordering: Both status_bar and command_line use `TopBottomPanel::bottom`, stacking from bottom up. Declaration order: status_bar first, then command_line — so command_line sits above status_bar.

Key notes:
- Command line Enter detection uses fallback `has_focus()` check since `text_edit_singleline` retains focus
- `pending_dispatch` is set (not directly dispatched) — the application loop reads it next frame
- `handle_platform_output` may have different API in egui-winit 0.34 — use the `.platform_output` field

## Task List

1. **Create `src/ui/mod.rs`** — `UiSystem` struct with `new()`, `run()`, `set_scale_factor()`. Import all sub-modules.
2. **Create `src/ui/status_bar.rs`** — `pub fn draw(ctx, camera: &CameraState, input: &InputState)`.
3. **Create `src/ui/command_line.rs`** — `pub fn draw(ctx, cmd_state: &mut CommandState)`.
4. **Create `src/ui/toolbar.rs`** — `pub fn draw(ctx, _cmd_state: &mut CommandState)`.
5. **Create `src/ui/property_panel.rs`** — `pub fn draw(ctx, _world: &hecs::World)`.

## Dependencies

Step 4 (CommandState, CommandInput), Step 6 (InputState, CameraState)

## Verification

```bash
cargo check
```

UI will not render without the application loop (Step 12). Compilation is the primary verification.

## Exit Criteria

- [ ] `cargo check` passes
- [ ] `UiSystem` struct compiles with `egui::Context` and `egui_winit::State`
- [ ] All 4 panel draw functions compile with correct signatures
- [ ] Status bar displays X, Y, Zoom
- [ ] Command line has prompt, error display, and text input
- [ ] Toolbar is left-side 40px panel
- [ ] Property panel is right-side 180px stub

title: Fix: explode_block_insert does not rotate arc angles by block transform
description:
## Problem
In src/block/explode.rs:123-124 (and the duplicate in the SpawnArc push block at ~137-138), arc start_angle and end_angle are copied raw from the block definition. When a block has non-zero rotation, exploded arcs are correctly positioned but point in the wrong direction. A 0°–90° arc in a block rotated 45° explodes to 0°–90° instead of 45°–135°.

apply_to_point correctly handles rotation for the arc center; angles need the same treatment.

## Root Cause
explode_block_insert extracts only scale_x from the transform and uses apply_to_point for positional data. There is no apply_to_angle utility on Transform2D, so angles were missed.

## Fix
1. In the BlockEntity::Arc arm, transform angles:
   start_angle: (start_angle + transform.rotation.to_degrees()).rem_euclid(360.0)
   end_angle:   (end_angle   + transform.rotation.to_degrees()).rem_euclid(360.0)
2. Apply same fix to the duplicate angles in the tx.push(AtomicOp::SpawnArc) block
3. Consider adding Transform2D::apply_to_angle(angle_deg: f64) -> f64 helper
4. Add test: block with rotation=PI/2, arc 0°–90° → exploded arc 90°–180°

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exploding a rotated block with arc entities produces arcs at correct world-space angles
- Test with non-zero rotation covers this case
- All 669+ tests still pass
notes: Fix: extracted start_angle/end_angle into let bindings using transform.apply_to_angle() before spawning entity and pushing AtomicOp. Added Transform2D::apply_to_angle(angle_deg) helper that adds rotation (rad→deg) and normalizes to [0,360). Added 2 tests: (1) arc 0°→90° with 90° rotation → 90°→180°, (2) arc 300°→350° with 90° rotation wraps to 30°→80°. Build passes, all 672 tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed: added Transform2D::apply_to_angle(angle_deg) helper, wired into explode_block_insert's Arc arm for start_angle/end_angle. 2 new tests verify rotation (0°→90° with 90° rot → 90°→180°) and wrap-around (300°→350° with 90° rot → 30°→80°). Build passes, all 672 tests pass.

title: Fix take_transaction() default None — silently drops undo history
description:
## Bug: `take_transaction()` default `None` — silently drops undo history

**File:** `src/commands/mod.rs` L46-48

**Current code (L46-48):**
```rust
fn take_transaction(&mut self) -> Option<crate::history::Transaction> {
    None
}
```

**Problem:** If a developer adds a new `Command` that produces a `CommandResult::Complete` but forgets to override `take_transaction()`, the transaction is SILENTLY discarded — the operation completes, produces no undo history, and the user cannot undo it. This is a **fail-silent** design.

**Affected commands:**
- 8 commands already override it: Erase, Move, Copy, Rotate, Scale, Mirror, Offset, Line
- 3 stub commands (Circle, Arc, Polyline) return `CommandResult::Error` from `on_input()`, never `Complete`, so they can't reach this code path

**Fix:** Change the default to fail-loud:
```rust
fn take_transaction(&mut self) -> Option<crate::history::Transaction> {
    unimplemented!("Commands that return Complete must override take_transaction()")
}
```

The 3 stub commands (Circle, Arc, Polyline) need explicit overrides:
```rust
fn take_transaction(&mut self) -> Option<crate::history::Transaction> { None }
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Default `take_transaction()` uses `unimplemented!()` (fail-loud)
- [ ] CircleCommand overrides `take_transaction() -> None`
- [ ] ArcCommand overrides `take_transaction() -> None`  
- [ ] PolylineCommand overrides `take_transaction() -> None`
- [ ] `cargo check` passes
- [ ] Existing tests pass (no reachable code change for completable commands)
- [ ] All 8 existing overrides still work (no behavioral change)
notes: PR #32 review finding 5. Contracts-reviewer flagged this as a High-severity design issue: the default `None` return silently drops undo history when a new command returns Complete without overriding take_transaction(). Changing to unimplemented!() makes the omission fail loudly at runtime. The 3 stub commands (Circle, Arc, Polyline) that never return Complete must override explicitly with `None`.
close_reason: Changed take_transaction() default from None to unimplemented!() (fail-loud). Added explicit None overrides to 3 stub commands (CircleCommand, ArcCommand, PolylineCommand).

title: fix: acos NaN in tangent computation when d approx radius
description:
**Bug:** `acos(self.radius / d)` returns NaN when d is very slightly less than radius due to IEEE 754 float rounding.

**File:** `src/snap/candidate.rs:184`

**Reproduce:** Cursor positioned so d is approximately radius (e.g., on the circumference with float imprecision). `radius/d` can exceed 1.0, acos returns NaN, all downstream trig calls produce NaN coordinates in snap result.

**Guard at L182 (`if d >= self.radius`)** does not prevent this because rounding can produce `radius/d > 1.0` even when `d >= radius`.

**Fix:**
```rust
let cos_val = (self.radius / d).min(1.0);
let angle = cos_val.acos();
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Clamp added before acos call
- [ ] Test: cursor exactly on circle circumference produces valid (non-NaN) tangent points
- [ ] Test: cursor very close to circle boundary (within float epsilon) produces valid results
- [ ] Existing tangent tests still pass
- [ ] PR #25 comment addressed
notes: Fixed: acos NaN by clamping radius/d to 1.0 before acos(). Test: tangent_cursor_very_close_to_circumference (d=radius+1e-16). PR #25 branch. Commit: HEAD~0.

title: fix: arc midpoint wrong crossing 0/360 boundary
description:
**Bug:** Arc midpoint calculation uses arithmetic mean `(start + end) / 2.0` which fails for arcs crossing 0/360.

**File:** `src/snap/candidate.rs:254`

**Reproduce:** Arc from 350 to 10 (20 sweep) produces midpoint at 180 (opposite side of circle). Should be 0.

**Root cause:** `let mid_angle_deg = (self.start_angle + self.end_angle) / 2.0;` does not account for sweep direction.

**Fix:**
```rust
let sweep = self.end_angle - self.start_angle;
let mid_angle_deg = self.start_angle + sweep / 2.0;
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Sweep-based midpoint calculation implemented
- [ ] Test: arc(350, 10) midpoint = 0 -> (10, 0)
- [ ] Test: arc(270, 90) midpoint = 0 -> (10, 0)
- [ ] Existing arc tests still pass
- [ ] PR #25 comment addressed

title: Fix: Process textures_delta.free to prevent GPU texture leak
description:
## Context Brief

PR #13 review identified a high-severity bug: egui texture deallocations are never processed.

Current code in app.rs:
- ui_system.run() returns UiOutput with textures_delta (set + free)
- Only textures_delta.set is iterated for upload (lines ~206-213)
- textures_delta.free is completely ignored

The free list contains texture IDs that egui has deallocated (e.g., font atlas regeneration on DPI change, dynamic image unloading). Without freeing them, the egui_wgpu renderer leaks GPU texture resources, causing monotonic GPU memory growth over a session.

## Task List

1. After the textures_delta.set upload loop, iterate textures_delta.free
2. For each texture_id in free, call self.render_state.egui_renderer.free_texture(texture_id)
3. Verify cargo check passes clean
4. Optional: add a tracing::debug! log when textures are freed (for profiling)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] textures_delta.free is processed every frame
- [ ] No GPU texture memory leak over long sessions
- [ ] Font atlas regeneration and dynamic images work correctly
- [ ] No compiler warnings or errors
close_reason: Fixed: added loop over textures_delta.free calling egui_renderer.free_texture() after UI render pass. Verified: zero warnings build.

title: Fix: Add unconditional framebuffer clear before entity pass
description:
## Context Brief

PR #13 review identified a high-severity bug: no framebuffer clear when grid is invisible.

Current code in app.rs:
- Grid render pass uses LoadOp::Clear (line ~166)
- Grid pass is gated on if self.resources.grid.visible
- When grid.visible is false, the grid pass is skipped entirely
- Entity pass (LoadOp::Load) and UI pass (LoadOp::Load) then draw on top of undefined/stale swapchain content

This causes visual artifacts: frame blending, ghosting, or uninitialized pixel garbage when the grid is toggled off.

## Task List

1. Add a standalone clear-only render pass before the conditional grid pass
2. The clear pass should use self.resources.camera.clear_color
3. Keep the grid pass conditional but change it to also use LoadOp::Load (since clear already happened)
4. Entity pass and UI pass remain LoadOp::Load
5. Verify cargo check passes clean

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Framebuffer is always cleared each frame regardless of grid visibility
- [ ] Grid pass uses LoadOp::Load (not Clear)
- [ ] No visual artifacts when grid is toggled off
- [ ] No compiler warnings or errors
close_reason: Fixed: added unconditional LoadOp::Clear pass before grid/entity passes. Grid renderer changed to LoadOp::Load. Verified: zero warnings build.

title: Add zoom guard to CameraState::screen_to_world and world_to_screen
description:
## Summary

**Severity:** 🟡 High
**File:** src/ecs/resources.rs:60-61, 79-80
**Found in:** PR #2 review

## Problem

`screen_to_world()` (L60-61) and `world_to_screen()` (L79-80) divide by `self.zoom` directly without a `.max(0.0001)` guard. The sibling method `view_proj_matrix()` (L117) correctly applies this guard, but the two coordinate conversion methods do not.

If `zoom` is `0.0` (possible before camera initialization in ForgeApp::new), f64 division by zero produces ±inf, and subsequent math produces NaN. NaN is contagious — it propagates into the command system, UI coordinate display, and all downstream state.

## Fix

Add `let z = self.zoom.max(0.0001);` in both methods and use `z` for division instead of `self.zoom`.

```rust
let z = self.zoom.max(0.0001);
Point2D::new(
    self.target.x + ndc_x * half_w / z,
    self.target.y + ndc_y * half_h / z,
)
```

## Verification

```bash
cargo check
cargo test
```

Add unit test: construct CameraState with zoom=0.0, call screen_to_world — should return finite coordinates, not NaN.
close_reason: Fixed: commit on feature/forge-x6t — added zoom guard to screen_to_world. PR #2 updated.

title: Step 10 — Entity Renderer (Lines/Circles/Arcs/Polylines)
description:
## Context Brief

The entity renderer (§7.4) renders all ECS entities with `Renderable` components:
- **Batching:** All entities of the same type are packed into one vertex buffer per frame → one draw call per entity type
- **Line Rendering:** Each `LineData` → 2 vertices, `LineList` topology
- **Circle Rendering:** Each `CircleData` → 64-segment line strip approximation, `LineStrip` topology
- **Arc Rendering:** Each `ArcData` → proportional segments based on sweep angle, `LineStrip`. Angles converted from degrees to radians for GPU.
- **Polyline Rendering:** Open → `LineStrip`, Closed → `LineList` (with closing segment)
- **Entity vertex format:** `{position: [f32; 2], color: [f32; 4]}` — shared across all types
- **Staging buffers:** Separate per type (`line_staging`, `circle_staging`, `arc_staging`, `polyline_staging`), each with capacity tracking (`*_staging_capacity`). Initial size: `INITIAL_STAGING_SIZE = 32768` bytes. Resize strategy: double capacity if exceeded.
- **WGSL shaders:** All use the same `CameraUniform` from `shared.wgsl`. Pipeline uses `LineList` or `LineStrip` primitive topology.

## Task List

1. **Create `src/render/shaders/line.wgsl`** — Same vertex/fragment structure as grid shader, using `CameraUniform` from shared WGSL.
2. **Create `src/render/shaders/circle.wgsl`** — Same structure; note that circle tessellation is done on CPU side.
3. **Implement `EntityRenderer::new()`** in `src/render/entity_renderer.rs`:
   - Load 4 WGSL shaders via `include_str!()`
   - Create 4 render pipelines (line: LineList, circle: LineStrip, arc: LineStrip, polyline: LineList)
   - All use `camera_bind_group_layout` for group(0)
   - Create 4 staging buffers, each 32KB initially
   - Set all capacity fields to `INITIAL_STAGING_SIZE`
4. **Implement `EntityRenderer::render()`**:
   - Query ECS for each entity type using hecs queries
   - For lines: iterate, generate 2 vertices per entity (start, end)
   - For circles: iterate, generate 64 vertices per circle (line strip approximation)
   - For arcs: iterate, generate proportional segments (sweep_angle/360 * 64, min 8)
   - For polylines: iterate vertices, add closing segment if `closed`
   - Write to staging buffers (resize by 2× if capacity exceeded)
   - Begin render pass for entities (load = `LoadOp::Load`, draw on top of grid)
   - For each type: set pipeline, bind camera bind group, set vertex buffer, draw
5. **Add degree-to-radian conversion note** in arc rendering: `angle * std::f64::consts::PI / 180.0` before computing vertex positions.

title: Step 09 — Grid Renderer with WGSL Shader
description:
## Context Brief

The grid (§7.3) is a single vertex-buffered line list, regenerated when camera position/zoom changes ≥10%:
- `GridRenderer::new()` creates the WGSL shader module (`grid.wgsl`), pipeline layout (using `camera_bind_group_layout`), render pipeline, and empty vertex buffer
- `render()` checks if grid needs regeneration, generates vertex data, writes to GPU buffer, and issues draw call
- Grid regeneration computes visible world bounds from camera, generates line vertices for major/minor grid lines within bounds + margin
- Axis lines (X=0, Y=0) use distinct color
- `last_target` and `last_zoom` fields track camera state for ≥10% change detection
- `invalidate()` forces regeneration on next render

## Task List

1. **Create `src/render/shaders/grid.wgsl`** — Full WGSL shader from spec (§7.3):
   - `VertexInput` with `@location(0) position: vec2<f32>`, `@location(1) color: vec4<f32>`
   - `VertexOutput` with `@builtin(position) clip_position: vec4<f32>`, `@location(0) color: vec4<f32>`
   - `@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> view_proj: mat4x4<f32>`
   - `vs_main` and `fs_main` functions
2. **Implement `GridRenderer::new()`** in `src/render/grid.rs`:
   - Load `grid.wgsl` shader source via `include_str!()` (embed at compile time)
   - Create shader module, pipeline layout, render pipeline with `LineList` primitive
   - Create empty vertex buffer (start with 32KB)
   - Initialize `last_target` and `last_zoom` to defaults
3. **Implement grid generation logic** — helper function `generate_grid_vertices(camera, grid) -> Vec<GridVertex>`:
   - Compute visible world bounds from camera target + viewport size + zoom
   - Add 10% margin, generate minor/major grid lines and axis lines
   - Each line segment = 2 vertices with position + color
   - Clamp total vertices to prevent buffer overflow
4. **Implement `GridRenderer::render()`**:
   - Check if camera moved ≥10% (compare `last_target`/`last_zoom` to current)
   - If changed, regenerate grid vertices
   - Write vertex data to GPU buffer (resize if needed)
   - Begin render pass with `LoadOp::Clear` (using `camera.clear_color`)
   - Set pipeline, bind camera bind group, set vertex buffer, draw

title: Step 06 — Input System (Mapper + Actions)
description:
## Context Brief

The input system (§8.1) maps winit events to application actions:
- `InputMapper` holds `state: InputState` and `last_mouse_screen: (f32, f32)`
- `handle_event(&mut self, event: &WindowEvent, camera: &CameraState) -> Vec<InputAction>`
- Maps `CursorMoved` → `InputAction::MouseMoved(Point2D)` (updates `InputState.mouse_screen` and `mouse_world`)
- Maps `MouseInput` (Pressed) → `Click`, sets `left_down`/`middle_down`/`right_down`
- Maps `MouseInput` (Released) → clears button states
- Maps `MouseWheel` → `InputAction::Zoom`
- Maps `KeyboardInput` (Pressed) → `Cancel` (Escape), `Confirm` (Enter), `Text(char)` (single chars), modifier key state (`shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`)
- Includes pan handling: when `middle_down`, computes delta from `last_mouse_screen` to current and produces `InputAction::Pan`

- `Text(char)` is dead code in v0.1.0 — egui swallows keyboard when its text field has focus

title: Step 05 — LINE Command Implementation
description:
## Context Brief

The LINE command (§6.3) uses a buffer-then-commit pattern:
- Points accumulate in `pending_points: Vec<Point2D>` (not spawned into ECS until confirmed)

- Text input "U" undoes the last point
- `steps_remaining()` returns 0 when ≥2 points accumulated (enables auto-commit for inline commands like "LINE 0,0 100,100")

title: Step 04 — Command Trait, CommandState, and nom v8 Parser
description:
## Context Brief

The command system (§6.1) defines:
- `Command` trait with methods `name()`, `prompt()`, `steps_remaining()`, `on_input()`, `on_cancel()`, `preview()`
- `CommandInput` enum: `Point(Point2D)`, `Text(String)`, `Distance(f64)` (dead_code), `Angle(f64)` (dead_code), `Cancel`, `Confirm`
- `CommandResult` enum: `Continue`, `Complete`, `Error(String)`, `Cancelled`
- `CommandState` struct: `active: Option<Box<dyn Command>>`, `history: Vec<String>`, `buffer: String`, `last_error: Option<String>`, `pending_dispatch: Option<String>`
- `PreviewEntity` struct: `points: Vec<Point2D>`, `color: Color`, `width: f32`

The parser (§6.2) uses nom v8's function-based API with `Parser` trait and `.parse()` method calls. Key functions:
- `parse_point(&str) -> IResult<&str, Point2D>` — parses "10,20" style coordinates
- `parse_command(&str) -> IResult<&str, ParsedCommand>` — dispatches on command name
- `ParsedCommand` enum with `Line(LineArgs)`, `Circle(CircleArgs)`, `Arc(ArcArgs)`, `Polyline(PolylineArgs)`
- Each `*Args` struct uses `Option` fields for inline arguments

Important parser details:
- Case-insensitive command names with aliases (LINE/L, CIRCLE/C, ARC/A, PLINE/PL)
- Whitespace after command name is optional (`opt(space1)`) to allow bare "LINE"
- `space1` after name prevents "LINE0,0" false matches
- PLINE close token "C" requires whitespace or EOF after it to avoid matching "C10,20" as a vertex
- PLINE returns error if no vertices collected
- ARC start_angle and end_angle are conditional on previous arg presence

title: Step 03 — ECS Components & Resources
description:
## Context Brief

ECS components (§5.2) are plain structs that implement `Send + Sync + 'static` (hecs 0.10 does not require a derive macro — any type satisfying these bounds is automatically a component). Key types:

- `Renderable` — marker struct (no fields)
- `Position(Point2D)` — placeholder for v0.2.0+ transforms
- `LineData { start, end: Point2D, color: Color, width: f32 }` — Copy
- `CircleData { center: Point2D, radius: f64, color: Color, width: f32 }` — Copy
- `ArcData { center: Point2D, radius: f64, start_angle, end_angle: f64, color: Color, width: f32 }` — Copy (angles in degrees)
- `PolylineData { vertices: Vec<Point2D>, closed: bool, color: Color, width: f32 }` — Clone (not Copy, heap-allocated)

ECS resources (§5.3) are singleton data structs:
- `CameraState` — `target: Point2D`, `zoom: f64`, `viewport_size: (u32, u32)`, `clear_color: Color`. Implements `screen_to_world(screen: (f32,f32)) -> Point2D`, `world_to_screen(world: Point2D) -> (f32,f32)`, `view_proj_matrix() -> Matrix4<f32>` with nalgebra's `Orthographic3`. Clones.
- `GridConfig` — `visible: bool`, `major_spacing, minor_spacing: f64`, `major_color, minor_color, axis_color: Color`. Has `Default` impl with visible=true, spacing 100/10, gray colors.
- `InputState` — `mouse_screen: (f32,f32)`, `mouse_world: Point2D`, `left_down, middle_down, right_down, shift, ctrl, alt: bool`. Derives `Default`.

## Task List

1. **Create `src/ecs/components.rs`** — All 6 component structs with appropriate derives. Add the design note comment for `Position`. Add the hecs note comment explaining no derive macro needed.
2. **Create `src/ecs/resources.rs`** — `CameraState`, `GridConfig`, `InputState` structs. Implement `CameraState` methods: `screen_to_world`, `world_to_screen`, `view_proj_matrix`. Implement `Default` for `GridConfig`. Implement `Default` for `InputState`.
   Key implementation details for `CameraState`:
   - `view_proj_matrix()` uses `nalgebra::Orthographic3::new(left, right, top, bottom, -1.0, 1.0)` with bounds computed from `target` and `zoom`
   - `screen_to_world()` normalizes screen coords to [-1,1] with Y flip, then inverts the projection
   - `world_to_screen()` is the forward transform
   - Both methods guard against zero viewport size and zero zoom
3. **Update `src/ecs/mod.rs`** — `pub mod components; pub mod resources; pub use components::*; pub use resources::*;`

## Dependencies

Step 2 (Point2D, Color)

## Verification

```bash
cargo check
```

title: forge-5s3.2: Missing test coverage — evaluate(t) out-of-range + to_polyline(0) panic

## Source
PR #37 test-coverage reviewer (C1 + I1). src/geometry/spline.rs.

## Problem
1. **Critical**: `CubicBezier::evaluate(t)` has no input validation for `t` outside [0,1] or NaN. Out-of-range `t` produces silently wrong points that may cause NaN vertices in wgpu render pipeline → GPU timeouts or undefined rendering.
2. **Important**: `to_polyline(0)` panic is documented but has no `#[should_panic]` test to lock in the contract.

## Recommendation
- Add `debug_assert!((0.0..=1.0).contains(&t))` in `evaluate()`
- Add test for out-of-range t values: `t=-1.0`, `t=2.0`, `t=f64::NAN`
- Add `#[test] #[should_panic(expected = "segments must be > 0")]` for `to_polyline(0)`

Also missing: zero scale, negative scale (mirroring), degenerate curve, center() on empty bbox.

## Severity
P2 — evaluate() gap can cause GPU instability; to_polyline(0) is P4 contract enforcement.

title: Fix per-frame staging buffer allocation in WindowSelectRenderer
description:
## Problem

PR #30 review found that `WindowSelectRenderer::render()` allocates a new 264-byte GPU staging buffer via `device.create_buffer()` on **every frame during drag** (window_select_renderer.rs L259).

The docstring says "persistent staging buffer" but the code creates a new one each time. This causes unnecessary GPU memory churn on the hot path.

## Fix

1. Add `staging_buffer: wgpu::Buffer` field to `WindowSelectRenderer` struct
2. Create the buffer once in `new()` with size 264 (11 vertices x 24 bytes)
3. In `render()`, use `queue.write_buffer` on the stored buffer instead of `device.create_buffer()`
4. Remove `device` parameter from `render()` signature (no longer needed)

## Files

- `src/render/window_select_renderer.rs` - main change
- `src/render/mod.rs` - update `render()` call site if signature changes

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Staging buffer created once in `new()`, reused every frame
- [ ] `render()` no longer takes `device` parameter
- [ ] All existing tests still pass
- [ ] Visual behavior unchanged (rect still renders correctly during drag)
close_reason: Persistent staging buffer created once in new(), reused in render() via queue.write_buffer. device parameter removed from render() signature. 434 tests pass.

title: Fix SCALE point-to-point reference distance heuristic
description:
## Problem

src/commands/scale_cmd.rs:L223-236 —  heuristic for point-to-point scale is non-standard and confusing for CAD users.

In AutoCAD/FreeCAD, point-to-scale uses a *reference length* workflow (pick two points to define the reference, then a third to define the new length). The current heuristic — average distance from base to all entity geometry — produces surprising results:
- Scaling a line from (0,0)→(10,0) with base at origin and click at (5,0) gives factor = 5/5 = 1.0 (no change)
- Click at (5,0) with base at (20,0) gives factor = 15/avg_dist — highly dependent on entity layout

## Fix

Either:
1. Disable point-to-point for v0.2.0, only support text input
2. Implement proper reference-length workflow: first click = base, second+third click = reference distance, fourth click = new distance

## Source

PR #29 code review finding
close_reason: Removed confusing compute_reference_distance heuristic. SCALE now only accepts text factor input. Point-to-point returns error directing user to type factor. 2 new tests added. Closes PR #29 code review finding.

title: fix: f64::EPSILON too tight for geometric tolerance
description:
**Issue:** `f64::EPSILON` (~2.2e-16) is machine epsilon, not a geometric tolerance. Floating-point trig easily produces errors larger than this.

**Files:** `src/snap/candidate.rs:85,100,154,197,217,285`, `src/geometry/point.rs:29`

**Specific problems:**
- L197: Tangent coincidence check will almost never trigger — tangent points computed via trig differ by > 2e-16 even when coincident
- L100: Degenerate line detection is too strict
- L154/L217: Zero-radius circle/arc guards are too strict
- Tests use 1e-9 but production uses f64::EPSILON — mismatch

**Fix:** Extract a domain constant:
```rust
const GEOMETRIC_EPSILON: f64 = 1e-9;
```

Replace all f64::EPSILON in geometric comparisons with GEOMETRIC_EPSILON. Keep f64::EPSILON for actual machine-epsilon use cases.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] GEOMETRIC_EPSILON constant defined
- [ ] All geometric comparisons use GEOMETRIC_EPSILON
- [ ] Tests aligned to use same tolerance
- [ ] Existing tests pass with new tolerance

title: fix: rank_by_priority ignores distance for same-priority candidates
description:
**Issue:** `rank_by_priority` sorts by snap-type priority only. Same-priority candidates (e.g., two Endpoint candidates from different polyline segments) are ordered by insertion order, not proximity.

**File:** `src/snap/filter.rs:65`

**Impact:** The first generated candidate wins, not the closest one. For a polyline with 10 segments, the Endpoint from segment 0 wins even if segment 9's Endpoint is closer to the cursor.

**Fix:** Add secondary sort by distance:
```rust
candidates.sort_by(|a, b| {
    let pa = priority_map.get(&a.snap_type).copied().unwrap_or(u8::MAX);
    let pb = priority_map.get(&b.snap_type).copied().unwrap_or(u8::MAX);
    pa.cmp(&pb)
        .then_with(|| a.distance_world.partial_cmp(&b.distance_world).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
});
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Composite sort key: priority first, distance second
- [ ] Test: two Endpoint candidates — closer one wins
- [ ] Test: Endpoint at distance 50 beats Nearest at distance 5 (priority still dominates)
- [ ] Existing filter tests still pass
- [ ] PR #25 comment addressed
close_reason: Fixed: rank_by_priority now uses composite key (priority, distance_world). Same-priority candidates ordered by world-space distance (closest first).

title: SpatialIndex query methods bypass ensure_clean()
description:
**Discovered:** PR#20 review (H2). **File:** src/spatial/mod.rs:137-171

title: SpatialIndex::insert() clears dirty flag — latent bug
description:

Remove line 118 (`self.dirty = false;`). Callers must use `ensure_clean()` explicitly after all modifications.

title: EntityRenderer robustness — empty polyline guard, buffer edge case, radius-based tessellation
description:
## Robustness improvements identified in PR#11 review

### Empty polyline guard (~L453)
Polyline vertex generation does not guard against `vertices.is_empty()`. An empty `PolylineData` would generate 0 vertices and produce an invalid buffer range.

### Buffer resize formula edge case (~L496-500)
`new_size = old_size.max(required_size) * 2` -- on the first overflow where `old_size < required_size`, this doubles the required size. That's fine, but if `required_size` is very large (e.g. a single giant polyline), the buffer could grow much larger than needed.

### Radius-dependent circle segments
`CIRCLE_SEGMENTS = 64` is hardcoded and resolution-independent. For tiny circles (radius < 1 world unit), 64 segments is overkill. For huge circles (radius > 1000), 64 segments looks jagged. Should compute segments as `clamp(radius * scale_factor, 8, 256)` or similar.

### Acceptance
- [ ] Add early return / skip for empty polylines in `render()`
- [ ] Review buffer resize logic for edge cases (exactly-at-capacity, massive single entity)
- [ ] Make circle/arc segment count depend on radius and zoom level
- [ ] Add unit tests for edge cases

### Source
PR#11 review findings.
close_reason: All 3 robustness items addressed: empty polyline guard added, buffer resize formula clarified, hardcoded CIRCLE_SEGMENTS replaced with radius×zoom dynamic tessellation (clamped [8,256]). 12 unit tests added, all 58 tests passing.

title: EntityRenderer performance — eliminate per-frame allocations and pipeline deduplication
description:
## Performance optimizations identified in PR#11 review

### 4x intermediate Vec allocations per frame (~L321-324)
Each entity type allocates a temporary `Vec` to collect vertices before uploading to the GPU:
- `line_vertices`, `circle_vertices`, `arc_vertices`, `polyline_vertices`

At 10,000 entities, this creates ~200,000 small Vec allocations per frame. Pre-allocate with `with_capacity` or reuse a persistent scratch buffer.

### Pipeline layout duplication (~L207-226)
All 4 pipelines use the exact same layout (camera_bind_group_layout). Could share a single `PipelineLayout` instead of creating 4 identical ones.

### Shader file deduplication (~L229-234)
`line.wgsl` and `circle.wgsl` are byte-for-byte identical except for comments. Could use one shared shader file (`entity.wgsl`) for both LineList and LineStrip primitives.

### Acceptance
- [ ] Pre-allocate vertex vectors with estimated capacity per type
- [ ] Benchmark frame time at 10,000 entities before/after
- [ ] Share a single `PipelineLayout` across all 4 pipelines
- [ ] Consider unifying `line.wgsl` and `circle.wgsl` into one file

### Source
PR#11 review findings.
close_reason: All three performance improvements implemented: single PipelineLayout, unified entity.wgsl, scratch buffers + push generators. cargo check: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

title: Step 12 — Application Loop (ForgeApp + ApplicationHandler)
description:
## Context Brief

The application loop (§10) ties all systems together:
- `ForgeApp` owns: `world: hecs::World`, `resources: ResourceBank` (camera + grid), `command_state: CommandState`, `render_state: RenderState`, `ui_system: UiSystem`, `input_mapper: InputMapper`
- `ForgeApp::new(window)` initializes all systems, using `pollster::block_on` for GPU init
- `ForgeApp::render(window)` orchestrates the frame: get surface texture → create encoder → update camera uniform → grid pass → entity pass → UI pass → submit
- `ForgeApp::dispatch_command_text(text)` parses input, dispatches to active command or starts new command
- `ForgeApp::recover_device(window)` stubs GPU recovery

`ForgeAppHandler` implements `ApplicationHandler`:
- `resumed()`: Create window and `ForgeApp`. Drop prior state first (macOS resume guard).
- `window_event()`: Handle lifecycle (CloseRequested, Destroyed, Resized, ScaleFactorChanged) → dispatch pending command text → egui consumes event → input mapper → process actions → request redraw
- `about_to_wait()`: Continuous redraw via `request_redraw()`

Key event dispatch flow:
1. Pending command text dispatched first
2. egui gets first chance to consume events
3. Remaining events → `InputMapper::handle_event` → `Vec<InputAction>`
4. `Click` → active command's `on_input(Point(...))`

title: forge-5s3.2: Public fields on new geometry types break encapsulation invariants
description:
## Source
PR #37 contracts reviewer (M2-M3). Multiple files.

## Problem
All new geometry types have all fields `pub`:
- `Transform2D { pub scale_x, scale_y, rotation, translate_x, translate_y }` — callers can construct with NaN, Inf, or zero scale
- `CubicBezier { pub p0, p1, p2, p3 }` — callers can construct with NaN control points
- `BoundingBox2D { pub min, pub max }` — callers can construct reversed min/max

`Transform2D::new()` and `BoundingBox2D::from_points()` exist but provide no enforcement since fields remain public. All invariants are violable by direct struct construction.

## Recommendation
Either: (a) make fields private, expose accessors + constructors only, or (b) add `normalized()` / `validate()` methods and document that direct construction must maintain invariants. Option (b) is lighter touch for a CAD geometry lib where direct field access is idiomatic.

## Severity
P3 — defensive design gap. No current callers exploit these backdoors, but as the API surface grows the risk increases.
close_reason: Resolved in PR #37 follow-up

title: forge-5s3.2: Transform2D missing Default impl despite IDENTITY const
description:
## Source
PR #37 code reviewer (M1). src/geometry/transform.rs:41.

## Problem
`Transform2D` defines `IDENTITY` as a public const but does not implement the `Default` trait. Inconsistent with the rest of the codebase — `PropertySource`, `PropertyValue`, `CubicBezier`, `LayerTable`, and `BlockTable` all implement `Default`. Users who want to use `Transform2D::default()` or `..Default::default()` in struct update syntax will hit a compile error.

## Recommendation
Add manual `Default` impl:
```rust
impl Default for Transform2D {
    fn default() -> Self { Self::IDENTITY }
}
```

Note: Cannot use `#[derive(Default)]` because IDENTITY has non-zero scale.

## Severity
P3 — usability gap, no functional impact.
close_reason: Resolved in PR #37 follow-up

title: forge-5s3.2: to_polyline() unbounded allocation — OOM crash risk
description:
## Source
PR #37 security auditor (M1). src/geometry/spline.rs:81-90.

## Problem
`to_polyline(segments: usize)` allocates `Vec::with_capacity(segments + 1)` without an upper bound. Passing `usize::MAX` or even a large value like `100_000_000` causes instant OOM crash. Any unsaved drawing work is lost.

## Recommendation
Add a maximum segment cap (e.g., `const MAX_SPLINE_SEGMENTS: usize = 10_000;`) and return `Result` or clamp, with a warning when cap is hit.

## Severity
P3 — self-DoS only (local desktop app), but causes irreversible data loss (unsaved work).
close_reason: Resolved in PR #37 follow-up

title: forge-5s3.2: Transform2D::new() uses Point2D for scale — type misuse footgun
description:
## Source
PR #37 contract reviewer (H1). src/geometry/transform.rs:64.

## Problem
`Transform2D::new(translate: Point2D, rotation: f64, scale: Point2D)` — both `translate` and `scale` parameters are `Point2D`, a type that semantically represents a *position*. A scale factor is a dimensionless multiplier pair. A caller who writes `Transform2D::new(scale, rot, translate)` compiles silently and produces subtly wrong transforms.

## Recommendation
Replace `scale: Point2D` with `scale_x: f64, scale_y: f64` or tuple `scale: (f64, f64)` which disambiguates caller intent by making the parameter type differ from `Point2D`.

## Severity
P3 — compile-time footgun, no runtime crash but silent wrong behavior.
close_reason: Resolved in PR #37 follow-up

title: Low polish: coordinate overflow guard, zero-viewport guard, redundant field, multi-GPU
description:
## Context
PR #9 review found four low-severity items worth tracking:

**L1:** f64→f32 cast in projection matrix can produce ±∞ at extreme coordinates (>1e38). Add clamp at parser level or in camera.

**L2:** No zero-viewport guard in `build_view_projection_matrix()` — defense-in-depth. Resize handler already guards, but camera method is public.

**L3:** Redundant `surface_format` field — exists in both `RenderState` struct and `config.format`. Remove the field, use `config.format`.

**L4:** `InstanceDescriptor` uses `display: None` — may misbehave on multi-GPU systems.

## Exit Criteria
- [ ] L1: Coordinate bounds documented or clamped
- [ ] L2: Zero-viewport guard added in camera
- [ ] L3: Redundant field removed
- [ ] L4: Multi-GPU behavior documented
close_reason: L1: f64→f32 overflow clamp, L2: zero-viewport guard, L4: multi-GPU docs. L3 already done in forge-bp4. cargo check passes. Commit f70af4d.

title: Add negative coordinate and edge-case float tests for nom parser
description:
## Summary

**Severity:** Low
**Found in:** PR #3 review
**Source:** forge-ucr (Step 04)

## Problem

The 16 parser unit tests cover positive coordinates and standard spacing but miss:
- Negative coordinates (e.g. LINE -10,-20 30,-40 — common in CAD)
- Scientific notation floats (e.g. CIRCLE 1e2,2e2 5e-1)
- CIRCLE with partial args (center only: CIRCLE 50,50)
- ARC with partial args (center + radius only: ARC 0,0 50)
- Trailing whitespace after args (LINE 0,0 100,100 with trailing spaces)

nom float handles negative/scientific notation correctly, but these cases are untested.

## Fix

Add 5-6 test cases to src/commands/parser.rs covering:
1. Negative coordinates in LINE and PLINE
2. Scientific notation float in CIRCLE/ARC radius
3. CIRCLE partial: center=Some, radius=None
4. ARC partial: center=Some, radius=Some, angles=None
5. Trailing whitespace: remaining should be empty or whitespace-only

## Verification

cargo test -- commands::parser
close_reason: 7 edge-case tests added (negative coords, scientific notation, partial args, trailing whitespace, PLINE C). All 23 parser tests passing.

title: forge-5s3.2: Incomplete clippy fix — 2 remaining clone_on_ref_ptr sites in history/mod.rs

When `cargo clippy` runs in CI, these two locations will still trigger warnings. 6 of 8 sites fixed — 2 remaining.

## Severity
P4 — cosmetic, no behavioral impact. But inconsistency means CI clippy still warns.
